questions.q: Why might a multinational company need more than one accounting representation of the same business events?
options: To intentionally make its books harder for auditors to read
Because different accounting standards, like local GAAP and IFRS, can require genuinely different treatment of the exact same underlying event
Because Oracle requires every company to maintain at least two ledgers
Because subledger transactions must always be entered twice
questions.explain: Different standards can require different depreciation methods, revenue timing, or account structures for the same events, which one representation alone cannot satisfy.

questions.q: How does Oracle Fusion deliver multiple accounting representations without duplicating subledger transactions?
options: By requiring the transaction to be manually re-entered once per ledger
By running two completely separate installations of Oracle Fusion
By disabling Subledger Accounting entirely for secondary ledgers
By entering the subledger transaction once and letting Subledger Accounting generate accounting for that single event into more than one ledger, each with its own accounting method
questions.explain: A transaction is entered once, but SLA can account for that one event into a primary ledger and one or more secondary ledgers, each governed by its own method.

questions.q: What actually differs between a primary ledger's representation and a secondary ledger's representation of the same event?
options: The accounting method assigned to each ledger, built from different AADs suited to each standard
The underlying transaction data itself, such as the amount or date
Nothing; both representations are always identical
Only the ledger's functional currency
questions.explain: The transaction data is identical across representations; what differs is the accounting method (and its underlying AADs) assigned to each ledger.

questions.q: In the worked example, what caused the primary and secondary ledgers to produce different depreciation entries for the same asset?
options: A data entry error on one of the ledgers
The asset was purchased twice
Random variation with no underlying cause
Each ledger's accounting method, built around a different standard's Fixed Assets AAD, applying different depreciation rules to the same asset addition event
questions.explain: The same asset addition event was accounted differently in each ledger because each ledger's accounting method used a different AAD suited to its accounting standard.

questions.q: Which earlier course concepts does multiple accounting representations rely on most directly?
options: Supporting references and description rules only
Journal import and Transfer Journal Entries to GL only
Mapping sets exclusively
Accounting methods (lessons 3 and 12) and ledger-level method assignment (lesson 13)
questions.explain: This lesson explicitly ties multiple accounting representations back to accounting methods and the ledger-level assignment of those methods covered earlier.
